about.summaryTitle: About the Pomodoro Technique: Science, Ultradian Cycles & FAQ
about.methodDesc: The Pomodoro Technique is an evidence-backed time-management method created by Francesco Cirillo. It organizes focused effort into structured 25-minute work sprints separated by 5-minute cognitive rest intervals.
about.boundary: Productivity Note: This timer is an educational tool designed to support cognitive pacing and sustainable focus. Adapt session intervals to fit your personal workflow and energy levels.
about.desc25: Singular focus on a single task without multitasking or notification interruptions.
about.desc5: Step away from screens, stretch, and allow dopamine reserves in the prefrontal cortex to replenish.
about.desc4Cycles: After 4 consecutive pomodoros, take a 15–30 minute break to reset executive attention.
about.faq1Q: Q: Why is 25 minutes the standard Pomodoro length?
about.faq1A: A: 25 minutes is brief enough to resist procrastination and distractions while providing enough sustained time to reach a state of productive flow.
about.faq2Q: Q: How do ultradian rhythms relate to periodic breaks?
about.faq2A: A: Nathaniel Kleitman's Basic Rest-Activity Cycle (BRAC) shows human energy naturally fluctuates. Scheduled micro-breaks align with these neurological peaks and valleys.
about.faq3Q: Q: Can I adjust interval times in settings?
about.faq3A: A: Yes. Use the Settings icon to configure custom work durations, short break times, and long break intervals according to your study or work demands.
about.faq4Q: Q: Is my productivity data saved privately?
about.faq4A: A: Always. All session counts, daily streaks, and custom settings remain 100% on your device in local storage. No tracking data is sent to external servers.
